title: Quebec separatism in the 'elbows up' era
summary: With the election of the Parti Québécois in Quebec, Canada will have its first separatist government in over a decade. How much trouble will it cause for Mark Carney?

image.caption: Parti Quebecois Leader Paul St-Pierre Plamondon waves to supporters after winning the provincial election in Montreal, on Monday, Oct. 5, 2026. THE CANADIAN PRESS/Graham Hughes (The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: With the election of the Parti Québécois in Quebec, Canada will have its first separatist government in over a decade. How much trouble will it cause for Mark Carney?
Front Burner28:15Quebec separatism in the 'elbows up' era
With the election of the Parti Québécois in Quebec Monday night, it's the first time in twelve years that Canada will have a separatist government in power.

Over the course of the campaign, the party's leader, Paul St-Pierre Plamondon, made clear some of the fights he could take up with Ottawa, over issues like immigration. He also vowed to hold a referendum on separation in his first term, a promise he doubled down on this week despite only securing a minority government.

With the Alberta referendum coming up, this means Mark Carney is now dealing with separatist movements on both ends of the country, at a time when he's trying to lead a united front against U.S. aggression.
Montreal-based journalist Martin Patriquin joins us to talk about what this election means for the country right now.
